title: Propagation dynamics of high-gain vortex beams in symmetry-broken media via forward and backward three-wave mixing
authors: Fan Meng, Hao Zhu, Xin-Yao Huang, Guo-Feng Zhang
abstract: In recent years, vortex light, a distinctive form of structured light, has attracted considerable attention owing to its unique properties and the rich physical phenomena arising from its interaction with matter. In this paper, we investigate the propagation dynamics of vortex beams in a symmetry-broken three-level system based on forward and backward three-wave mixing (TWM) processes. We find that both processes enable the transfer of high-gain vortex light, with the associated topological charges obeying identical algebraic relations. The forward process exhibits periodic oscillatory transmission and modulates the transverse spatial profile of the generated signal vortex field, whereas the backward process features stable transmission and produces a signal field with higher gain and improved fidelity. Under the Autler-Townes splitting (ATS) regime, the probe field detuning in both schemes has a negligible influence on the gain. Optical depth influences only the rate at which the gain approaches its maximum, while the peak value remains unchanged. These results constitute a meaningful extension of the work reported in reference [40] and may provide a feasible approach for quantum communication, quantum computation, and the generation of high-gain, high-fidelity vortex light.
summary: This paper analyzes the dynamics of vortex beams propagating through a three-level atomic medium using forward and backward three-wave mixing. By comparing both processes, the authors demonstrate that the backward TWM scheme is superior for generating high-gain, high-fidelity structured light. The findings suggest practical applications in quantum communication and computation utilizing OAM.
main_problem: The study investigates how high-gain vortex beams propagate through symmetry-broken media using both forward and backward three-wave mixing (TWM) processes.
main_result: Backward TWM was found to yield superior performance compared to the forward process, exhibiting higher signal gain, improved fidelity, and more stable transmission characteristics.
method: The authors employed a perturbative approximation and steady-state assumption to solve the coupled Maxwell-Bloch equations derived from the system Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The model is a three-level ladder-type atomic system exhibiting broken inversion symmetry, driven by a strong control field ($\omega_c$) interacting with weak probe ($\omega_p$) and signal ($\omega_s$) fields.
key_observables: Vortex light properties, including topological charge (OAM), gain, fidelity, transmission characteristics, and spatial profile modulation.
important_parameters: The analysis focuses on the Autler-Townes Splitting (ATS) regime; detuning ($\Delta_p$) has a negligible influence on gain, while optical depth only affects the rate of reaching maximum gain.
main_assumptions: Key assumptions include treating the control field as strong and continuous ($|\Omega_c| \gg |\Omega_p|, |\Omega_s|$), using the perturbative approximation, and assuming steady-state conditions ($\partial/\partial t = 0$).
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the symmetry-broken three-level ladder system setup. Figure 2 likely shows relative intensities of probe and signal fields during forward propagation under varying decay rates.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model using a Hamiltonian, derives coupled equations of motion via the Liouville equation, applies approximations to simplify these equations, and then solves the resulting steady-state Maxwell-Bloch equations for both Forward TWM (FTWM) and Backward TWM (BTWM).
why_interesting: This work directly addresses quantum optics phenomena—specifically structured light propagation and nonlinear interactions in atomic media—which are foundational to developing integrated photonic components for quantum communication.
